newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia scraps vote in 10 towns, citing violence.
newsitem.headline: Colombia scraps vote in 10 towns, citing violence.

text.p: Residents of 10 Colombian towns won't vote in forthcoming nationwide municipal elections because of growing threats of violence from leftist rebels, the country's electoral registration board said Monday.

Electoral registrar Orlando Abello announced that voting would be canceled in the 10 towns but said the move affected less than 0.5 percent of Colombia's voters, who are spread across some 1,100 municipalities.
The towns affected are mostly in southern Caqueta province and eastern Meta province.

In some communities the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Latin America's oldest rebel force, banned anybody standing as candidates for the post of mayor and municipal councilors in the elections set for Oct. 26.
In other cases the FARC and the smaller Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN) forced registered candidates to step down.
Both rebel forces and right-wing paramilitary gangs have threatened to kill any opposing political candidates who dare to campaign in their zones of influence.

Towns covered by the cancellation order include Cartagena del Chaira, in Caqueta, where FARC rebels released 70 soldiers, some of whom they had been holding prisoner for more than nine months, in a public ceremony in June. The poll has also been shelved in the nearby town of Valparaiso.
In the last month, rebels killed one ruling party senator in northeast Norte de Santander province and kidnapped and later released five mayors in southern Narino province.

The ELN has also been blamed for the kidnapping of at least 12 town councilors and local government officials in northern Bolivar province over the weekend. Police said the officials are still missing.
President Ernesto Samper said last week he would consider using emergency powers to appoint serving military officers as mayors in areas where local elections could not be held.
